description: Cases for the size-split sub-issue trust rule (admit.mjs splitChildBody, owner Q93 with the Q9 extension): a body counts as the listed human's text only when the lanes App wrote it, its native parent was filed by a listed human, its header names that parent, and either nobody edited it and every line after the header is one of the parent's trusted task-list lines (lines starting with the admission rules' `task-list`, `- [ ] `), or a listed human last edited it and every line after the header is one of those lines or that line with its box ticked (`- [ ] ` written `- [x] ` or `- [X] `, the rest unchanged). GitHub names only the last editor, so that edit vouches only for ticked boxes. An edit by any other account leaves it untrusted. A header whose third line is `<!-- size-split refinement=<id> updated_at=<time> -->` (its part line then reads "copied from #N and intake's refinement comment on it as written") also allows that comment's task-list lines, never its other lines, on both paths and with the same ticked forms after a listed human's edit, and counts at all only while that comment is still the parent's newest refinement (the lanes App's comment opening with `<!-- intake-triage refinement -->`), never edited (last_edited_at null), with updated_at equal to its created_at or to the recorded time, on a parent body a listed human wrote; this holds even when a listed human edited the child. Actors are {type, id} with type User or Bot; parent is the child's native parent number or null; size is the triage Size. admit.test.mjs and resolve-pr.test.mjs read this file. child.parent is null or {number, repo}, repo as owner/name and absent for this repository; a parent elsewhere never counts. A parent's comments, oldest first, are {id, author, body, created_at, updated_at, last_edited_at, editor}, id the REST and GraphQL databaseId. A case-level app_id overrides the top-level one, and null means the reader has no lanes App id, so nothing counts.
